summary: The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says that from 15 September 2026 nationals of 60 countries and territories are entitled to visa exemption for tourism for up to 30 days, and its summary of the revised schemes lists Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia as eligible for a visa on arrival. Tourist visas are applied for online at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' e-Visa website, thaievisa.go.th, and the Immigration Bureau says all passengers must complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC).

The visa is for remote workers, digital nomads and freelancers and for participants in activities such as Muay Thai courses and Thai cooking classes; spouses and dependent children of DTV holders are also eligible. tips.text: The UK government says overstaying brings a fine of 500 baht a day up to a maximum of 20,000 baht, and that you risk being held in detention, deported at your own expense and banned from re-entering Thailand for up to 10 years.

The UK government says it is illegal to possess or use any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heat-not-burn device in Thailand, and that offences can lead to confiscation, heavy fines, detention and court proceedings.

The UK government says criticising the Thai monarchy ('lèse-majesté') is illegal, that the law can be interpreted broadly and carries a long prison sentence, and that journalists, human rights defenders and members of the public have faced charges for making political comments or sharing articles online.

The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is submitted on the Immigration Bureau's site, tdac.immigration.go.th, which says foreigners are required to submit their arrival card information 3 days in advance of their arrival date in Thailand.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Thailand?
faq.answer: No. The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says that from 15 September 2026 nationals of 60 countries and territories, the USA among them, are entitled to visa exemption for tourism for up to 30 days. The Immigration Bureau says all passengers must complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card, and that foreigners are required to submit their arrival card information 3 days in advance of their arrival date.

faq.question: What is the TDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Thailand Digital Arrival Card is the arrival card submitted online at tdac.immigration.go.th, the Immigration Bureau's site. It says all passengers must complete it, and that foreigners are required to submit their arrival card information 3 days in advance of their arrival date in Thailand.

faq.question: How much does a Thailand tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: Through the Royal Thai Embassy in Washington, the single-entry tourist visa costs USD 40 and the multiple-entry tourist visa, valid for 6 months from the date of issuance, USD 200; the Embassy says applications are made online only at www.thaievisa.go.th. It says nationals of the 60 countries and territories under the Tourist Visa Exemption Scheme are entitled to visa exemption for tourism for up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I extend my visa-free stay in Thailand?
faq.answer: The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says the 30-day visa-exempt stay for tourism can be extended for another period not exceeding 30 days, at the sole discretion of the immigration officer. The UK government tells British nationals that if they want to stay longer they must get the appropriate visa before they travel or, if eligible, apply for an extension through the Thai immigration authorities, and get any extension they need before their permission expires.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Thailand?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance an entry requirement for tourists. The Royal Thai Embassy in Washington says certain types of visas (O-A and O-X) require the applicant to submit a Foreign Insurance Certificate.
